info.name: ldsr Wallet Service
info.description:
Wallet service with user accounts and transfers between wallets.

Set baseUrl, adminEmail and adminPassword in an ENVIRONMENT, one per target. Tokens, identifiers and idempotency keys are collection variables written by the request scripts; nothing needs pasting by hand.

Requests that replay an idempotency key have no pre-request script and reuse a key variable owned by exactly one other request, so running things out of order cannot break them.

Amounts are integer minor units (kobo): 100000 is 1,000 naira.

request.description: Liveness plus a real database connectivity check.
Creates the account and its wallet in one transaction. Returns 409 if the account already exists; use Login user A instead.
Deliberately does not set accessToken. Admin stays explicit so nothing inherits it by accident.
karmaone@ldsr.com, karmatwo@ldsr.com and karmathree@ldsr.com are seeded into the blacklist, so this works on a freshly seeded database with no manual setup.
Schemas are strict, so an unknown field is refused rather than silently dropped.
Indistinguishable from a wrong password, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts.

request.description: 100000 kobo is 1,000 naira. Generates creditKeyA, which the replay below reuses.

item.name: Credit wallet A again with the same key

request.description: No pre-request script, so it reuses creditKeyA. Only Credit wallet A changes that variable, so this holds regardless of what else you run in between.
Uses its own key variable, so it cannot disturb the replay above.
A user able to credit their own wallet could mint money.
No fromWalletId in the body: the source is derived from the authenticated caller. Generates transferKey, reused by the two requests below.

item.name: Transfer again with the same key

request.description: Reuses transferKey. Identical body, so the original result is returned.
Reuses transferKey with a different amount. Returning the original result would report that a 500.00 transfer succeeded when only 250.00 moved.
422 rather than 400: the request is well formed, the outcome is not permitted.
Refused rather than rounded. Silently rounding somebody's money is worse than refusing the request.

item.name: Screen existing users against the blacklist

request.description: Reports accounts that appear on the blacklist. On a seeded database this finds flagged@ldsr.com, an account that was opened before it was blacklisted. Registration screening cannot catch that case.

exec: pm.test('found at least one match', () => pm.expect(d.count).to.be.above(0));

request.description: Screening reports; blocking is a separate explicit decision. Re-run the screen afterwards and the status reads BLOCKED.

item.name: [negative] Cannot transfer to a blocked account

request.description: Blocking stops funds in both directions, so no balance accrues that its owner cannot reach.
The caller expresses a desired state, not a transition, so repeating it is not an error.
Run Login admin first, which captures adminUserId.
